key_insight: A simplified Phan-Thien-Tanner (sPTT) fluid exhibits a purely elastic centre-mode instability in both channel and pipe flows, implicating transient rheology rather than steady flow properties.
engineering_relevance: The findings suggest that inertia-free instabilities may arise under realistic viscoelastic flow conditions and help distinguish constitutive models for engineering simulations.
method: Numerically analyse linear stability of pressure-driven sPTT channel and pipe flows.
Identify centre-mode instability in the absence of inertia.
Compare predictions with Oldroyd-B and FENE-P models.
evidence_signal: The numerical study finds instability across a wide range of polymer concentrations and at much lower Weissenberg numbers than previously predicted, despite sPTT and FENE-P sharing identical steady rheology and laminar profiles.
watch_item: The abstract reports linear numerical predictions, not experimental confirmation or proof that the instability develops into sustained chaotic flow.
paper_title: Purely elastic centre-mode instability in channel and pipe flows of a simplified Phan-Thien-Tanner fluid
